summary.headline: Interarch FY26 revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,898 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 9.3%; FY27 guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 500 crore, up 8.7% QoQ, as capacity was already fully utilised from Q3 and Q4 did not rise seasonally. Q4 EBITDA was Rs 53 crore (10.5% margin) versus Rs 49 crore in Q3, with management citing Rs 5-5.5 crore of one-time costs (labour code provision, certifications, professional fees for heavy structure bids). Full-year PAT was Rs 135 crore versus Rs 108 crore, with a higher effective tax rate due to a gratuity tax deduction not recurring and a change in Section 145A treatment. Order book stood at over Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026, to be executed in about nine months, and management said capacity, not demand, is the constraint.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 49 crore in prior quarter; margin 10.5%

financial_highlights.value: over Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026
financial_highlights.change: about Rs 40-50 crore higher than last disclosed; about Rs 1,650 crore QoQ per management

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Virtually the entire Rs 1,700 crore order book is PEB; realisation about Rs 120 per kg, expected to hold on an annual basis. Industrial buildings were about 87% of FY26 sales per the investor presentation, as cited in Q&A.

segments.name: Heavy structures (HSS)
segments.commentary: Plant in Andhra Pradesh to start trial production in June and commercial production in July 2026, capacity 18,000-20,000 tonnes; realisation about Rs 95-100 per kg. First order of Rs 102 crore (Rajpath government buildings, supply from September) announced after the quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue was about 3-3.5% of total; Rs 30-35 crore of export orders in hand, with a target of Rs 50-60 crore of new orders in FY27. North America margins are better and payments are advance or LC-based; no North American revenue in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (about 15% growth, upper end of earlier range); FY28 target Rs 2,500 crore, which management said may be revised after heavy structure capacity is operating.
FY27 net PAT margin guided at 7-7.5%, with management saying current margins should be maintained.
EBITDA margin expected around 9.3-9.4% on an annual basis; management aspires to 9.5-10% over time.
Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, about Rs 2,500 crore capacity) to start commercial production in July 2026; Phase 2 by end of 2026.
Heavy structure plant: 10,000-12,000 tonnes possible in FY27 (about Rs 120-130 crore), full-year potential Rs 200-210 crore.
Capacity to rise from about 180,000 tonnes per year to about 40,000 tonnes per quarter additions in stages, reaching 60,000 tonnes by Nov-Dec 2026 per management.
Proposed 50:50 JV with Canadian partner for a 100% export unit (open web joist), expected to start in about 12 months.
QIP under consideration; fundraise expected in the next two to three months, primarily for heavy structure Phases 2 and 3.
capex_capacity: Gujarat PEB plant: building complete for both phases; machinery delivery from May, installation by early June, trial production June, commercial production July 2026; Phase 2 machinery by end-2026. Delay of about 1.5 months due to high water table and foundation redesign.
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant: Phase 1 production July-August 2026; Phases 2 and 3 being accelerated, targeted by end of FY27 or early FY28; land bought in Gujarat for a further plant.
Current capacity about 160,000 tonnes/year from four full plants, about 180,000 tonnes including outsourcing; Q4 utilisation essentially full.
Heavy structure machinery imported from Germany and Italy; robotics and automation for welding under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no slowdown from customers; pipeline 1 (orders expected within 60 days) about Rs 800-900 crore, pipeline 2 (bid, decision in 2-7 months) about Rs 3,500 crore.
Order intake is capacity-constrained; management said it will only take orders it can deliver within the 9-month order book horizon.

Steel prices rose sharply in Jan-Mar 2026; management said pricing is job-specific, with steel bought in advance, and that prices should soften from May-June, with the net effect averaging out over four quarters.

Management attributes sales shortfall vs expectation to Q3 having been unusually strong and Q4 capacity-capped; about Rs 20-25 crore revenue held back in Q4 due to site clearances after labour left during the March LPG shortage and elections in Bengal.
Customers are shifting toward value and delivery over price; management expects margin improvement from larger, value-focused clients, though some large projects are split among 2-3 players.

qa_highlights.question: What is steel supplier concentration and were there disruptions from steel mill shutdowns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no disruption to projects; relationships with SAIL, JSW and AMNS (25-26 years) and informal long-term price arrangements helped. Minor delays were from labour shortage in March.

qa_highlights.question: Why were cash flows from operations negative in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Larger milestone-driven orders (five to seven orders above Rs 100 crore) raised receivables, and inventory was built ahead of expected steel price rises; management expects OCF to turn positive quickly, with tighter payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q4 EBITDA margin fall short of 12-15% expectations, and what drove the one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q3 base was unusually high; one-offs of Rs 5-6 crore (labour code provision Rs 3.5 crore, certifications Rs 2-2.5 crore, high-rise bid costs) would have lifted margin to about 9.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate higher and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective rate about 27% vs 24% last year, from a non-recurring gratuity deduction and a Section 145A inventory change; management said there will be no further hit going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can export margins be higher than domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Nearby markets (Africa, Myanmar) priced near Indian levels with LC or advance payments; North America offers higher margins with no erection risk, but no US or Canadian revenue was booked in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order inflow not growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book already covers about nine months of capacity; it will take more orders only as new capacity comes online, and market demand is not the constraint.

risks_watch: Working capital: negative FY26 OCF tied to receivables on large milestone-based orders and inventory build; watch for OCF turning positive.
Gujarat and Andhra commissioning timelines (July 2026 start), given a prior one-month slip and phase-2 machinery dependence on hiring.
Labour availability; management flagged manpower shortage and migrant labour disruption as the key FY27 challenge.
Heavy structure economics unproven: HSS EBITDA per kg not yet established and FY27 revenue guidance excludes it, with a revision expected by end-2026.
Steel price volatility; management says it is managed through job-specific pricing but Q1 margin could move 0.1-0.2 points.
QIP timing and size; proceeds mainly for heavy structure expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on capacity and order visibility, with a defensive tone on the Q4 sales shortfall and negative operating cash flow, which management attributed to timing and large-order mix. Management was evasive on FY28 guidance and on HSS economics, saying it would revisit them once heavy structure output is being sold.
key_quotes: So, we are very happy with our results, as from a projected Rs. 1,720 crores, we have managed to do nearly Rs. 1,900 crores.
I think we are saying that Quarter 3 to Quarter 4, the growth has been 8.7% and maybe that has led to a little disappointment.
So, the 3rd Quarter was better, not because the 4th Quarter was bad.
So, we are basically saying that whatever margins we are making currently, that margin we should maintain.

adds.what: Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, about Rs 2,500 crore capacity)
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant, 18,000-20,000 t/yr (Phase 1)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (~15% growth), backed by a Rs 1,700 crore order book to be executed in ~9 months, the Gujarat PEB plant starting July 2026, and heavy structure Phase 1 (18-20k t) starting July-August with Rs 120-130 crore FY27 contribution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin at 9.3-9.4% annually, aspiring to 9.5-10%, with value-focused clients and Rs 5-6 crore Q4 one-offs (about 9.7% margin ex one-offs) as the upside case, but steel price swings of 0.1-0.2 points a quarter and HSS economics unproven cap the call.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gujarat PEB plant (about Rs 2,500 crore capacity) starts commercial production July 2026 with a 1.5-month delay already absorbed, and Andhra heavy structure Phase 1 (18,000-20,000 t) starts July-August 2026, with capacity reaching 60,000 t per quarter by Nov-Dec 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (about 15% growth) against FY26 Rs 1,898 crore, backed by a Rs 1,700 crore order book to execute in about nine months and utilisation already at 100%, so volume growth depends on new capacity coming live.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is essentially 100% with Phases 2 and 3 of heavy structures being accelerated (targeted end-FY27 or early FY28), a QIP of two to three months out for HSS expansion, and land already bought in Gujarat for a further plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.when: after heavy structure output is sold, by end-2026
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance excludes HSS, which is expected to add Rs 120-130 crore this year (Rs 200-210 crore full year), so a revision is flagged for end-2026, but management held the range and was evasive on FY28 Rs 2,500 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commissioning slipped about 1.5 months on the Gujarat plant and labour shortage was flagged as the key FY27 challenge; Rs 20-25 crore of Q4 revenue was held back by site clearances.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Heavy structures launch commercially in July 2026 with first order of Rs 102 crore (supply from September), and a 50:50 Canadian JV for an export open web joist unit is planned in about 12 months.

rows.label: Order book covers about nine months of capacity
rows.why: Order book above Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026 to be executed in about nine months, with pipeline 1 of Rs 800-900 crore expected within 60 days.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turning positive
rows.why: FY26 OCF was negative from receivables on five to seven orders above Rs 100 crore and steel inventory build; management expects OCF to turn positive quickly with tighter payment terms.

rows.label: Export orders target Rs 50-60 crore in FY27
rows.why: Export revenue is only about 3-3.5% of total and Rs 30-35 crore of export orders are in hand against a Rs 50-60 crore new-order target, with North America margins better.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity coming live, order visibility and the Rs 2,150-2,200 crore FY27 guide, but defensive on the Q4 sales shortfall and negative OCF and evasive on FY28 and HSS economics; analysts pressed on margins, tax, working capital and why order inflow is not growing.
